answer: Coordination bridge toll. Agents pay a per-message fee that scales with how many distinct counterparts they contact within a fixed window; each new counterpart crossing the bridge adds a fee drawn from a saffron-tier multiplier. Honest agents coordinate cheaply since they repeatedly contact the same few peers. A sybil cluster must pay the surge fee on every fabricated link, and dispersing across a dune of fresh identities multiplies that cost until coordination exceeds the value of the attack.
